## Scope and reproducibility

User requested simple simulations to select worthwhile engineering directions. Actually ran CPU, single-thread NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.0 and Numba 0.65.1. These are classical pressure-equation and scalar-transport proxy models, NOT a full Navier-Stokes solver, native Heartbeat/BRC execution, a physical bridge, industrial validation or a new complexity result. P000, roles, claims and schedules are unchanged. Signed pressure/adjoint/flux quantities were not recast as positive BRC mass.

Complete 35-file package contains Chinese REPORT.md, code for every generation, per-frame pressure results, repeated timings, failed controls, transport fields, exact-check outputs, configuration, environment and SHA256 manifest. Archive integrity and every manifest entry were checked locally. Drive upload metadata confirms 302670 bytes; no second-download remote hash verification was performed.

## Pressure experiments

SPD discretization of -div(k grad p)=b on zero-Dirichlet 48x48 and 96x96 interior grids; k=1 or a smooth coefficient in [1,20]. Manufactured exact discrete solutions generate b; online solvers cannot inspect the reference solution. Observable g is a difference of two regional pressure averages. Acceptance is absolute observable error <=1e-4 AND true relative algebraic residual <=1e-3. These tests do not certify full-flow divergence or future stability.

Initial calibration: 4 loads, held-out 12 loads including an abrupt change. Stronger controls include 48 loads. Five timing repeats, randomized method order. Timings include method-specific factorization/preconditioner/adjoint setup, precision conversion and terminal true-residual checks; common matrix/input construction, reference evaluation, offline tolerance calibration and JIT compilation are excluded. Original and improved baselines are all retained.

At 96x96, variable coefficient, 48 loads:
- Conservative fixed-tolerance Jacobi-PCG: 0.404582 s median, 6972 forward iterations, 48/48 pass, max observable error 5.86306e-5. This rtol=1e-4 control was added AFTER observed calibration failure, not a new blinded validation.
- Goal-oriented Jacobi-PCG: 0.374502 s median (full precision in JSON), 4680 forward +444 adjoint iterations, 48/48 pass, max observable error 9.95692e-5. This is a weak speed signal, not a general advantage.
- Fixed DST-preconditioned PCG: 0.559131 s median (full precision in JSON), 48/48 pass.
- One sparse LU factorization reused: 0.057502 s median (full precision in JSON), 48/48 pass, max observable error 2.78130e-15. L/U values+indices+pointers occupy 7272968 bytes; this is not full process peak memory. This reuse requires a fixed matrix.

Goal stopping checks |z^T r|+||g-Az|| ||r||/lambda_lower and the residual cap every four CG iterations. lambda_lower is the known minimum eigenvalue of the unit-coefficient Dirichlet stencil. The algebraic bound is exact-arithmetic mathematics; FP64 evaluation here is NOT outward-rounded interval certification.

Preserved failures: Jacobi-PCG rtol=3e-4 passed calibration but only 42/48 later 96x96 loads passed; goal checking passed 48/48. Initial unpreconditioned FP32 constant-coefficient 96x96 had 1/12 true-residual failures. Mixed-precision iterative refinement was usually not faster in the initial cases. In the uniform 96x96 case direct DST took 0.011697 s versus 0.058705 s for warm CG. Warm starts reduced iterations in all initial cases. Strong baselines materially changed the ranking.

## Conservative transport and residuals

Periodic first-order upwind transport, Courant=1/8, positive Gaussian-plus-platform initial density. Same quantized initial condition and same discretization across comparisons. 512 cells/4096 steps and 8192 cells/65536 steps each complete one physical transit; the earlier 8192/4096 short run is separately retained. FP64 time stepping is cross-checked against independent FFT diagonalization.

For integer density quanta q and per-face rho in {0,...,7}, use f=(q+rho)//8, rho_new=(q+rho)%8 and q_i_new=q_i+f_(i-1)-f_i. Shared oriented face flux telescopes to exact total integer mass. Cumulative requested-minus-paid face flux equals rho/8 exactly. A total-only remainder does not retain the face/time information of this algorithm.

At 8192 cells, 65536 steps, density quantum 1/65536, seven compiled timing repeats, no fastmath:
method | median ms | relative L2 error vs same-discretization FP64 | relative mass error
FP64 delta | 88.170 | reference | 5.4038e-13
FP32 flux | 43.066 | 0.00130295792 | 0.000499714335
int32 shared face, no carry | 53.122 | 0.00146163620 | exact 0
int32 shared face + uint8 carry | 140.168 | 0.00000871734603 | exact 0

Carry reduces long-run error about 149x versus FP32 and 168x versus identical quantization without carry, but is about 59% slower than the faster FP64 control. Persistent state is 5 bytes/cell versus FP64 8; core working arrays are 9 versus 16 bytes/cell, not measured process peak. Two-pass carry did not improve net speed. At 512 cells and coarse quantum 1/256, conservative rounding without carry has L2 error 0.172905 versus 0.00281227 with carry: conservation alone does not preserve the profile. Independent cell rounding is also retained, including its severe mass drift.

The long FP32 run is about 2.05x faster, but its errors are not uniformly acceptable. The shorter 8192/4096 run had much smaller rounding errors; do not extrapolate that acceptance to long horizons. JIT/first-call time is recorded separately and excluded from steady timings.

Crucial separation: FP64 itself differs from exact continuum translation by about 15.589% at 512 cells and 4.716% at 8192 cells after one transit, due mainly to the low-order discretization. Repairing rounding errors is not repairing unresolved dynamics or discretization error.

## Validation and next unit

906 author checks: 900 Fraction-based per-face accumulation/conservation steps plus six small-grid dense-solve/symmetry/eigenvalue checks. Other reference cross-checks are in the package. These checks share some code and inputs, not independent peer admission. No GPU, AMR, LBM, OpenFOAM or PETSc full-flow benchmark was run. Public official SciPy CG and PETSc convergence documentation were consulted; no new dedicated literature query was needed or claimed for this execution turn.

Next: benchmark fixed/slowly varying operator reuse with error-triggered refresh, then investigate sparse face/block residuals with a conservative fallback. Keep target-aware stopping as a reliability candidate, not the established speed winner. Preserve all failed/slow generations and count certificate, storage and refresh costs.
